name: Orvana Occasion Gown — Tail-Vent Standard
description:
Orvana's accessible line — distinct from their Spire couture — is designed for Tier 3 buyers who want genuine tailoring at a price that doesn't require financing. The Occasion Gown is floor-length, cut in a silk-analog that holds color well and resists static cling in the charged air of most Meridian indoor venues. The Tail-Vent Standard variant includes a structured rear panel that splits cleanly from mid-hip to hem, with internal tension bands that keep the split closed when standing and open naturally under movement. It accommodates most TESSERA standard-issue geneware tails without bunching or binding.

Orvana offers the gown in twelve colorways and four standard geneware configurations: tail-vent, wing-slit back, horn-clearance hood attachment, and standard. Custom configurations are available for an additional Φ40–Φ80. The construction is clean and the fit is reliable. It is not a statement piece — it is a dress that works, that lasts, and that doesn't make the wearer think about it during the event.
cultural_context: The Orvana Occasion line is the default formal purchase for Tier 3 geneware-modified individuals. It's common enough at mid-tier events that it reads as baseline rather than aspirational. Some people are proud of it; others find it slightly embarrassing to be wearing the same gown as three other people at the same function. Orvana has responded to this by expanding their colorway range annually.
story_hooks: At a corporate reception, the character is wearing the same gown in the same colorway as a TESSERA genomics consultant. The consultant assumes this means they work for TESSERA. The character doesn't correct her immediately.

The character's tail is a non-standard TESSERA modification — slightly longer and heavier than the spec the Tail-Vent Standard is designed for. The tension bands give out midway through an important event.

A fashion journalist from a Ringo lifestyle feed is doing a piece on 'the democratization of geneware fashion.' They want to photograph the character in the gown. The character has complicated feelings about being used as evidence of progress.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length formal gown with elegant simplicity and practical engineering. The silhouette is refined but unpretentious—fitted through the bodice and waist, flowing gracefully to the floor. The distinctive rear panel split creates an asymmetrical visual interest when in motion, while maintaining a clean, closed line when stationary. Reads as 'dressed up but not trying too hard.'
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the torso with a gentle taper at the waist, then flowing freely from hip to floor. The rear vent allows for natural stride without restriction. Designed to accommodate standard TESSERA geneware modifications—particularly tail integration—without visible strain or bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Silk-analog synthetic; high-quality, color-stable, and static-resistant for indoor venue environments.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, lustrous surface with a subtle drape. The fabric catches light evenly without shimmer. Internally, discrete tension bands at the vent provide structural reinforcement without visible seaming.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in twelve colorways—assumes a mid-tone jewel tone (emerald, sapphire, or deep rose) as baseline. Solid, non-patterned for professional versatility.
physical_description.closures: Likely invisible side zip or magnetic fastenings; clean lines suggest minimal visible hardware. Back vent managed by internal tension-release mechanism that responds to movement.
distinctive_features: Structured rear panel with clean mid-hip-to-hem split
Internal tension bands that maintain closure when standing, release under motion
TESSERA tail-vent accommodation—reinforced internal seaming around integration points
Static-resistant treatment visible as subtle surface finish
No visible branding; quality implied through fit and construction
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 accessible luxury. Not cheap, not expensive. Reliable middle-market formal wear.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of mid-tier corporate events, geneware-community gatherings, and professional social functions. Wearing one signals financial stability without conspicuous consumption. Common enough to be invisible, distinctive enough to suggest competence. May carry subtle social weight—some wear it with pride as 'good enough,' others experience mild embarrassment at ubiquity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to lightly worn. Orvana construction means it ages gracefully—no pilling, no fading, no visible stress at seams. A well-maintained gown can serve for multiple seasons.
